oil.summary: Crude sold off sharply across the board on Wednesday despite an active geopolitical backdrop: WTI dropped 2.55% to $92.19/bbl, Brent fell 1.37% to $97.89, while heating oil cratered 5.81% and RBOB shed 4.10%. The EIA's reported 3-million-barrel crude build drove the bearish session, overwhelming lingering Hormuz risk premium. Headlines from over the weekend flagged three tankers damaged in the Gulf and Iran maintaining its oil blockade, yet Gulf neighbors' exports remain partially shut while Iranian crude reportedly continues to flow. On the sanctions front, Trump's Russia legislation threatens 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil—putting India and China's combined ~2.1 million bpd imports under pressure—a theme expected to headline the September 24 Trump-Xi White House summit. Options markets now price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting.
drivers: Bearish EIA print: 3M barrel crude build pressured flat prices despite distillate stocks running 12% below seasonal average
Hormuz crisis partially priced in: tanker strikes and Iran's blockade threat offset by evidence Iranian barrels continue to move, capping upside
Russia sanctions/tariff legislation and China's 80% grip on Iranian oil set to dominate Trump-Xi summit agenda, adding geopolitical tail-risk

gas.summary: Henry Hub surged 6.95% on the day to $3.171/MMBtu, extending a strong weekly (+9.69%) and monthly (+13.98%) run, as the Hormuz crisis reshapes global LNG supply expectations. A dedicated analysis piece today warned that roughly 20% of global LNG supply must now be treated as interruptible following nearly seven months of Hormuz disruption—a structural shift that is rerating prompt gas. TTF was comparatively muted, adding just 0.78% to €73.915/MWh after last week's 5.27% pullback, suggesting European markets see less direct spot tightness for now. TotalEnergies' decision to develop the Ima offshore gas field in Nigeria to boost Nigeria LNG supply represents a supply-side response at the margin, but new volumes are a multi-year story. News flow for gas beyond the Hormuz LNG angle is thin today.
drivers: Hormuz LNG disruption risk: ~20% of global LNG supply now viewed as interruptible, driving Henry Hub sharply higher
TotalEnergies greenlights Nigeria Ima gas field development to expand NLNG capacity—bullish longer-term supply signal
TTF lagging HH rally, reflecting European market's relatively contained near-term spot exposure to Hormuz vs. Asian LNG buyers

power.summary: EU Carbon EUAs edged up just 0.08% to $82.505/EUA, consolidating a solid monthly gain of 5.10% while TTF ticked modestly higher. News flow directly relevant to European power and carbon is thin today. On the technology side, China broke ground on a hybrid facility using supercritical CO2 as a working fluid alongside molten-salt thermal storage—notable for long-run decarbonization trends but with no near-term price impact. A climate startup disclosed CO2 capture agreements with three unnamed U.S. oil producers, signaling that private-sector carbon capture deal-making is filling the void left by reduced U.S. federal incentives. Geopolitical noise around Russian sanctions and Ukraine war diplomacy (Jaishankar-Rubio talks in New York) provides background macro risk but has no direct read-through to EUA pricing today.
drivers: EUA market broadly stable; monthly uptrend intact at +5.10% but today's session nearly flat with limited fresh catalysts
Private carbon capture deal flow accelerating as U.S. federal incentives recede, with a startup signing agreements with three oil producers
China's supercritical CO2 power plant groundbreaking highlights emerging low-carbon technology but is a long-dated, not near-term, market factor
